faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtext: Everything you need to know about controller testing, stick drift, and browser compatibility.
faq.q1: How do I run a controller test online?
faq.a1: To run a controller test online: connect your controller via USB or Bluetooth, open the test page on ControllerTesting.com, and interact with your controller. The browser reads input through the standard Gamepad API. No download, no account, and no software installation is required.
faq.q2: Can I test a PS5 DualSense or PS4 DualShock controller online?
faq.a2: Yes. Connect your PS5 DualSense or PS4 DualShock 4 controller by USB or Bluetooth, then open the PS5 controller test or general drift detector. The browser exposes controller input through the Gamepad API on Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.
faq.q3: What does the gamepad tester check?
faq.a3: The gamepad tester suite checks: analog stick drift (to 0.1% precision), all buttons, trigger pressure curves, vibration motors, polling rate in Hz, stick circularity, deadzone thresholds, and input latency. Start with the Full Diagnostic for a complete 2-minute checkup.
faq.a4: Yes. All 39 diagnostic tools on ControllerTesting.com are free to use. No account is required, no data leaves your device, and no software needs to be installed — everything runs in your browser using standard Web APIs.
faq.q5: How do I know if my controller has stick drift?
faq.a5: Connect your controller, open the Stick Drift Detector at controllertesting.com/test/controller/drift, and let the sticks rest at center. A reading above 2% on either axis indicates drift. Values under 2% are typically within the clean range. The test shows drift to 0.1% precision in real time.
faq.q6: Does the controller test work on Xbox controllers?
faq.a6: Yes. Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, and Xbox One controllers work with the gamepad tester on Chrome, Edge, and Firefox via USB or the Xbox Wireless Adapter. Bluetooth Xbox controllers also work on most modern browsers.

seo.introParagraph: Whether you're a competitive esports player looking to eliminate input delay on controller games, or a casual gamer verifying a secondhand console to play the best nintendo switch games, hardware reliability is critical. From preparing for upcoming nintendo switch 2 games on the much-anticipated nintendo switch 2 console to enjoying classics on a nintendo switch oled or nintendo switch lite, having a fully functional gamepad is non-negotiable. Our platform provides an instant, installation-free controller test directly in your browser. Utilizing the HTML5 Gamepad API, we read raw telemetry from your hardware, allowing you to visualize analog stick accuracy, button actuation, and trigger linearity across all major devices—including the playstation 5 controller, the nintendo switch pro controller, and the xbox elite controller series 2.
seo.card1Title: Precision Diagnostics: Visualizing Stick Drift and Wear
seo.card1Text: Analog stick degradation is the most common point of hardware failure in modern gamepads. Before you invest in a costly nintendo switch joy con repair or buy a new set of nintendo switch games, it is crucial to determine if your crosshair movement is caused by a software deadzone configuration or physical potentiometer wear. Our diagnostic suite measures resting axis variance down to a 0.1% margin of error. If you are experiencing unexpected camera movement on your DualSense, running our dedicated test will quickly confirm the presence of ps5 controller drift, empowering you to adjust your in-game settings or pursue a warranty claim.
seo.card2Title: Supported Hardware: From Next-Gen to Retro
seo.card2Text: Our testing engine is built for maximum compatibility. You can perform a rigorous xbox controller test to verify the adjustable tension thumbsticks on an xbox elite controller (including the xbox elite controller series models), or map the unique inputs of a switch 2 pro controller. We extensively support nintendo hardware; whether you are testing a standard nintendo switch joy con or mapping a legacy super nintendo controller switch setup via USB, our interface accurately reflects the nintendo controller layout. Even an old nintendo controller or an original nintendo controller paired with an adapter can be analyzed for input latency and ghosting. If you need to test a joy con controller, a switch controller, or verify nintendo switch controller drift, we have you covered.
seo.card3Text: A frequent barrier to hardware testing and playing controller games for pc is establishing a stable connection. A common question we receive is how to connect ps5 controller to pc, how to connect ps5 controller generally, or how to connect ps5 controller to iphone. For PC, the most reliable method with the lowest latency is a direct USB-C connection. For wireless testing or iOS gaming, simply hold the Create and PS buttons simultaneously until the light bar flashes to initiate Bluetooth pairing. Once connected, your OS will expose the device to the browser, allowing you to instantly play online controller games (or pc controller games) or run our polling rate diagnostic on your ps5 controller pro or standard ps5 controller. We also fully support the xbox controller and ps4 controller for all these features.
seo.card4Text: While our ps4 controller test and ps5 controller test suites are highly accurate, it's important to understand the limitations of the Gamepad API. Browsers normalize inputs differently depending on your operating system. For example, Windows may apply a hardware-level deadzone to Xbox controllers before the data ever reaches the browser. Similarly, testing a nintendo controller switch setup, a joy con 2, or a switch joy con wirelessly via Bluetooth can introduce artificial latency compared to a wired connection. We always recommend using a wired connection on a Chromium browser (like Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge) for the most accurate diagnostic results across all your nintendo switch and next-gen gaming hardware.

glossary.title: Controller Hardware Glossary & Tips
glossary.driftDesc: Stick drift occurs when analog sticks register input without being touched. This is typically caused by physical wear in traditional carbon-film potentiometers. A deadzone is a software-level threshold (e.g., 5-10%) applied to ignore these microscopic false inputs.
glossary.hallDesc: Unlike traditional ALPS potentiometers, Hall Effect modules use magnetic fields to measure stick position. Because there is no physical contact or friction between the internal components, they are virtually immune to wear-induced stick drift, drastically extending the controller's lifespan.
glossary.pollingDesc: Polling rate is how often your controller sends data to your device, measured in Hertz (Hz). A standard Bluetooth connection yields around 125Hz (8ms latency). Overclocking or using a wired USB connection can push this to 500Hz-1000Hz (1ms-2ms latency), critical for competitive gaming.
glossary.circularityDesc: When you rotate a joystick along its outer edge, a perfect module should trace a mathematically perfect circle. Circularity error measures the deviation from this perfect circle. High deviations (>15%) can result in uneven diagonal movement speeds in FPS games.

methodology.collapsibleTitle: How this test works & its limits
methodology.point1: This test reads your controller through the browser's standard Gamepad API — no drivers, no installs, nothing leaves your device.
methodology.point2: Readings depend on connection mode: Bluetooth reports at lower rates than USB. Compare like-for-like (wired vs wired).
methodology.point3: We measure the input reaching the browser — display lag and game-engine queues are outside this test's view.
methodology.point4: A clean reading now does not guarantee no drift in-game: deadzones differ per game, and wear develops over time. Use the Drift Timeline to track yours.
methodology.point5: This is a diagnostic, not a hardware-lab certification. For repair or RMA decisions, confirm with a second run or second tool.

qh.whyTitle: Why Use the 60-Second Quick Controller Health Check?
qh.whyDesc: When buying a used controller, prepping for a tournament match, or troubleshooting sudden aim issues, you don't always have time for extensive manual testing. Our 60-Second Quick Health Check automates stick drift sampling, button responsiveness, and trigger pressure verification into four 15-second guided phases.
qh.p1: Phase 1: Stick Drift & Zero-Point Error: Measures resting thumbstick drift percentage and axis center offset.
qh.p2: Phase 2: Button Response Matrix: Confirms face action button (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle), D-pad, and shoulder bumper actuations.
qh.p3: Phase 3: Trigger Linearity: Evaluates L2/R2 analog trigger pressure from 0% resting to 100% full travel.
qh.p4: Phase 4: Express Score & Passport Record: Calculates an overall hardware score, awards 50 XP, and logs your test snapshot into your Controller Passport.
qh.faqQ1: What is the 60-Second Quick Health Check?
qh.faqA1: The Quick Health Check is an express 60-second guided diagnostic that tests stick drift, button matrix actuation, and trigger linearity in continuous guided phases.
qh.faqQ2: How is the Quick Health Score calculated?
qh.faqA2: The score (0-100) combines resting thumbstick zero-point drift %, face button matrix coverage, and L2/R2 analog trigger pressure travel.
qh.faqQ3: Can I save my Quick Health results to my Passport?
qh.faqA3: Yes! Upon completing the 60-second check, your results are automatically saved to your local Controller Passport history and award 50 XP.
